Implementation GoThru SSO API

Scope

Villume exposes two public endpoints backed by the same GoThru Keycloak authentication flow:

  • POST /v1/auth/gothru
  • POST /v1/register/gothru

The auth endpoint signs in an existing account. The register endpoint is a compatible entry point for clients starting from registration. Both endpoints can also link an existing Villume account or create a new account when needed.

Configuration

KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL=https://gothru-sso.web.id
KEYCLOAK_URL=https://gothru-sso.web.id
KEYCLOAK_REALM=gothru
KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE=villume-dev
JWT_SECRET=<villume-jwt-secret>

KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL is preferred. KEYCLOAK_URL is used only as a fallback. KEYCLOAK_REALM defaults to gothru.

KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE documents the configured API audience. The current implementation verifies the access token through Keycloak's userinfo endpoint, matching the Panorra reference flow, so it does not validate the audience locally.

Database migration

Apply pending migrations before enabling the endpoints:

go run -mod=mod ./cmd/migrate up

Migration 20260909000000_create_user_keycloak_link creates the identity-link table. It enforces one Keycloak identity per realm and one Keycloak link per Villume user. Its down migration removes only that table.

Request

POST /v1/auth/gothru
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "access_token": "<keycloak-access-token>"
}

token is also accepted as a compatibility alias:

{
  "token": "<keycloak-access-token>"
}

The register endpoint uses the same request body.

Authentication flow

  1. Villume sends the access token to {KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL}/realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/userinfo.
  2. Keycloak must return sub, a valid email, and email_verified=true.
  3. Villume first resolves the account using (realm_name, keycloak_sub).
  4. If no link exists, Villume links a local account with the same email.
  5. If no local account exists, Villume creates the user and required detail, notification, and mail rows.
  6. Villume stores or refreshes the Keycloak link in the same database transaction.
  7. Villume returns its own 30-day JWT. Clients use this JWT for later Villume API requests, not the Keycloak token.

Success response

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "messages": "Login success",
    "code": "success",
    "token": "<villume-session-token>",
    "user": {
      "id": "<villume-user-id>",
      "email": "user@example.com",
      "username": "username"
    }
  }
}

Error responses

  • 400: malformed body or missing access token
  • 401: rejected token, missing identity claims, invalid email, or unverified email
  • 403: inactive Villume account without a pending reactivation flow
  • 502: Keycloak is unavailable or returns another non-success status
  • 500: database, account-linking, or local-session failure

Implementation files

  • src/action/v1/auth/authKeycloak.go: token verification and account resolution
  • src/action/v1/auth/authShared.go: shared Villume session creation
  • src/controllers/v1/authController.go: controller entry point
  • src/routes/v1/authRoutes.go: endpoint registration
  • src/routes/v1/route.go: public-route exclusions
  • src/models/userKeycloakLink.go: GORM identity-link model
  • migrations/20260909000000_create_user_keycloak_link.*.sql: reversible schema change
  • api-collection/Villume GO/Auth/GoThru Login.yml: login request
  • api-collection/Villume GO/Auth/GoThru Register.yml: register request

Verification

go test ./...
go vet ./...

For an end-to-end check, set gothru_access_token in the selected API-collection environment and run either GoThru request. A successful request stores the returned Villume JWT in the collection's token variable.

Backend Contract

Every backend needs these values:

KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL=https://auth.gothru.co
KEYCLOAK_URL=https://auth.gothru.co
KEYCLOAK_REALM=gothru
KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE=villume-dev

For the current dev Keycloak server:

KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL=https://gothru-sso.web.id
KEYCLOAK_URL=https://gothru-sso.web.id
KEYCLOAK_REALM=gothru
KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE=villume-dev

KEYCLOAK_URL can be kept as a fallback alias for services that already read
that name. New services should prefer KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL.

Backend Login Endpoint

Expose a backend endpoint similar to Panorra's:

POST /auth/gothru
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "access_token": "<keycloak_access_token>"
}

Successful response should return the application's own session:

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "code": "success",
    "token": "<local_app_session_token>",
    "user": {
      "id": "local-user-id",
      "email": "user@example.com",
      "username": "username"
    }
  }
}

The local app token is not the Keycloak token. It is the token your own app uses
for API requests after login.

Backend Verification Options

Use one of these verification approaches.

Option A: Userinfo Verification

This is the simplest implementation and matches the current Panorra backend.

Backend pseudocode:

read access_token from request body
reject if missing

GET {KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL}/realms/{KEYCLOAK_REALM}/protocol/openid-connect/userinfo
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
Accept: application/json

if Keycloak returns 401 or 403:
  return 401 Unauthorized

if Keycloak returns non-2xx:
  return 502 Cannot verify GoThru token

read userinfo:
  sub
  email
  email_verified
  preferred_username
  name
  given_name
  family_name

find local user by keycloak sub
if not found:
  create or explicitly link local user

create local app session/JWT
return local app session/JWT

This works in any backend language because it is only an HTTP request to
Keycloak.

Option B: JWT/JWKS Verification

This is stronger and better for high-traffic APIs because the backend validates
the Keycloak JWT locally.

Backend requirements:

  • Fetch JWKS from:
    {KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL}/realms/{KEYCLOAK_REALM}/protocol/openid-connect/certs
  • Cache signing keys
  • Validate RS256 only
  • Validate issuer:
    {KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL}/realms/{KEYCLOAK_REALM}
  • Validate expiry
  • Validate audience when your Keycloak client is configured to include it
  • Use sub as the stable external user ID

Do not trust decoded JWT claims before signature validation succeeds.

User Mapping

Every app should store a link between the local user and Keycloak:

local_user_id
keycloak_sub
keycloak_email
keycloak_username
realm_name
linked_at

Use keycloak_sub as the stable identity. Email and username can change, so
they should not be the permanent link.

Recommended behavior:

  • Existing linked user: log in normally
  • New GoThru user: create local user or start onboarding
  • Existing local user with same verified email: link only if the product has
    approved this behavior
  • Unverified email: do not silently link accounts by email

Error Handling

Return safe, generic errors to the frontend:

Missing token -> 400
Invalid or expired token -> 401
Token verified, but local user is blocked -> 403
Backend cannot reach Keycloak -> 502
Unexpected app failure -> 500

Useful troubleshooting:

  • unauthorized_client: Keycloak client is probably confidential, has wrong
    redirect URI, or has invalid client settings for a public SPA.
  • Invalid client or Invalid client credentials: frontend is using a public
    flow against a client that requires a secret.
  • Cannot verify GoThru token: backend cannot verify the token with Keycloak.
    Check KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL, KEYCLOAK_REALM, network access, and token expiry.
  • aud is account: the token is valid for Keycloak account APIs. Configure an
    audience mapper if your backend validates a custom API audience.

Security Checklist

  • Use HTTPS in production.
  • Use authorization code flow with PKCE for browser/mobile apps.
  • Never store a Keycloak client secret in frontend code.
  • Treat access tokens like passwords. Do not paste them into tickets, chats, or
    logs.
  • Verify the token on the backend before creating an app session.
  • Use sub as the permanent external identity.
  • Validate token expiry.
  • Prefer JWKS validation for production APIs when possible.
  • Log diagnostic errors without logging full tokens or authorization headers.
  • Keep app session lifetime independent from the Keycloak access token lifetime.

Panorra Reference

Panorra PWA uses this pattern:

Angular callback route
  -> keycloak-js obtains Keycloak access token
  -> POST /auth/keycloak to app2-dev.panorra.com or app2.panorra.com
  -> Go backend calls Keycloak userinfo
  -> backend creates Panorra JWT
  -> frontend stores Panorra session

Other GoThru apps can keep the same contract while replacing Angular, Go, or
Fiber with their own framework.

Issue #187: GoThru SSO Logout API Implementation

Scope

Villume exposes two public logout endpoints backed by the GoThru Keycloak OIDC logout and revoke flows:

  1. POST /v1/auth/gothru/logout (Primary / Recommended endpoint for GoThru SSO)
  2. POST /v1/auth/logout (Generic alias, useful if frontend uses a generic auth service)

Both endpoints utilize the same underlying handler (GoThruLogout) to:

  • Terminate the active user session in Keycloak (so that subsequent SSO logins require credentials instead of automatically logging back in).
  • Revoke associated Keycloak tokens.

Configuration (Backend)

KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL=https://gothru-sso.web.id
KEYCLOAK_URL=https://gothru-sso.web.id
KEYCLOAK_REALM=gothru
KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE=villume-dev
  • KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL is preferred. KEYCLOAK_URL is used as a fallback.
  • KEYCLOAK_REALM defaults to gothru.
  • KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE is directly used as the Keycloak client ID (villume-dev). No new environment variables are required.

Frontend Integration Guide

1. Endpoint Reference

Endpoint Method Auth Header Description
/v1/auth/gothru/logout POST Optional (Public) Primary endpoint for GoThru SSO logout.
/v1/auth/logout POST Optional (Public) Generic alias for logout.

Note: Both endpoints are registered under AuthJWTExclude. The frontend can call them even if the Villume session JWT has already expired in the browser.

2. Request Payloads

Option A: Send refresh_token (Recommended)

Send the Keycloak refresh_token stored in the frontend upon login.

POST /v1/auth/gothru/logout
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "refresh_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
}

Option B: Send both refresh_token and access_token

If the frontend stores both, the API will terminate the Keycloak session using refresh_token and revoke the access_token simultaneously.

POST /v1/auth/gothru/logout
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "refresh_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
}

Option C: Compatibility Alias token

If the frontend stores only a single token variable:

POST /v1/auth/gothru/logout
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
}

Option D: Authorization Header Fallback

If the request body is empty, the API also extracts the token from the Authorization header:

POST /v1/auth/gothru/logout
Authorization: Bearer <keycloak-refresh-token>

4. Frontend Code Examples

A. Using fetch (TypeScript / JavaScript)

interface LogoutResponse {
  statusCode: number;
  data: {
    valid: boolean;
    messages: string;
    code?: string;
  };
}

async function logoutGoThru(): Promise<void> {
  const refreshToken = localStorage.getItem('gothru_refresh_token');

  try {
    const res = await fetch(`${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}/v1/auth/gothru/logout`, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        refresh_token: refreshToken,
      }),
    });

    const result: LogoutResponse = await res.json();
    console.log('Logout response:', result.data.messages);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Logout error:', error);
  } finally {
    // Always clear client-side auth tokens regardless of response
    localStorage.removeItem('token'); // Villume session JWT
    localStorage.removeItem('gothru_access_token');
    localStorage.removeItem('gothru_refresh_token');

    // Redirect user to the login page
    window.location.href = '/login';
  }
}

B. Using axios

import axios from 'axios';

async function handleLogout(): Promise<void> {
  const refreshToken = localStorage.getItem('gothru_refresh_token');

  try {
    await axios.post('/v1/auth/gothru/logout', {
      refresh_token: refreshToken,
    });
  } catch (err) {
    // If 401 (token already expired / invalidated in Keycloak), continue local cleanup
    console.warn('Keycloak session already expired or invalidated');
  } finally {
    localStorage.clear();
    sessionStorage.clear();
    window.location.href = '/login';
  }
}

Logout Flow & Sequence

  1. Frontend Request: The client calls POST /v1/auth/gothru/logout passing refresh_token.
  2. Token Validation: Villume validates the presence of a token. If none is found, returns 400 Bad Request.
  3. Keycloak OIDC Session Termination:
    • Villume sends POST /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/logout to Keycloak with client_id=villume-dev and refresh_token.
    • Keycloak invalidates the user session across the SSO Realm.
  4. Token Revocation (Optional):
    • If an access_token was also included, Villume calls /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/revoke to invalidate the access token.
  5. Success Response: Villume returns { statusCode: 200, data: { valid: true, messages: "Logout success", code: "success" } }.
  6. Frontend Cleanup: The frontend removes stored session tokens (token, gothru_refresh_token, etc.) and redirects the user to the login screen.

1. Environment & Endpoints Overview

Keycloak exposes two main categories of APIs:

  1. OIDC / OAuth 2.0 Endpoints: Mounted at /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/*. Used by frontend clients, mobile apps, and backend APIs for login, token issuance, user verification, and token exchange.
  2. Admin REST API: Mounted at /admin/realms/{realm}/*. Used by backend services, CI/CD, migration scripts, and administrative systems to manage users, groups, roles, and clients.

Configured Realms

Realm Description
master Primary administrative realm used to authenticate admin users and obtain admin management tokens.
gothru GoThru application realm containing all users, federations, clients (e.g. panorra-app, testingin), and roles.

Environment Base URL Realm Admin Console
Local Dev http://127.0.0.1:8180 gothru http://127.0.0.1:8180/admin
Dev Server https://gothru-sso.web.id gothru https://gothru-sso.web.id/admin

2. Authentication & Token Acquisition

2.1 Admin CLI Token (Password Grant)

Used by admin scripts, migration tooling, and CLI tasks to obtain a bearer token for the Admin REST API.

Endpoint:
POST /realms/{admin_realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token

cURL Request

curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/master/protocol/openid-connect/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "client_id=admin-cli" \
  -d "grant_type=password" \
  -d "username=admin" \
  -d "password=your_admin_password"

Response (200 OK)

{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
  "expires_in": 60,
  "refresh_expires_in": 1800,
  "refresh_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "not-before-policy": 0,
  "session_state": "b3e0c034-7164-4e38-9e6e-2144c8c73499",
  "scope": "profile email"
}

Note

Admin access tokens usually have a short lifetime (e.g., 60 seconds). For long-running batch jobs, refresh the token periodically using the refresh_token or re-authenticate.

2.2 Service Account Token (Client Credentials Grant)

Used for secure machine-to-machine (M2M) communication without a user context. The client must be configured with Client Authentication: ON and Service Accounts Roles: Enabled in Keycloak.

Endpoint:
POST /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token

cURL Request

curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/gothru/protocol/openid-connect/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "grant_type=client_credentials" \
  -d "client_id=backend-service" \
  -d "client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET"

Response (200 OK)

{

2.3 User Token (Authorization Code Flow with PKCE)

Used for Single Page Apps (SPA like Panorra PWA) and mobile clients.

Step 1: Generate PKCE Code Verifier & Challenge

  1. Generate high-entropy cryptographic random string (code_verifier).
  2. Calculate SHA-256 hash of code_verifier and Base64URL-encode it (code_challenge).

Step 2: Redirect User to Keycloak Login

Direct browser to:

https://gothru-sso.web.id/realms/gothru/protocol/openid-connect/auth?
  client_id=panorra-pwa&
  response_type=code&
  scope=openid%20profile%20email&
  redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.panorra.com%2Fcallback&
  state=xyz123random&
  code_challenge=E9Melhoa2OwvFrGMTJguCH5rtG6j3DwYZETb_6ecd80&
  code_challenge_method=S256

Step 3: Exchange Authorization Code for Tokens

Once redirected back to redirect_uri?code=AUTH_CODE&state=xyz123random, exchange code via POST:

curl -X POST "https://gothru-sso.web.id/realms/gothru/protocol/openid-connect/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "grant_type=authorization_code" \
  -d "client_id=panorra-pwa" \
  -d "code=AUTH_CODE" \
  -d "redirect_uri=https://app.panorra.com/callback" \
  -d "code_verifier=ORIGINAL_CODE_VERIFIER"

Response (200 OK)

{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1Ni...",
  "expires_in": 300,
  "refresh_expires_in": 1800,
  "refresh_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1Ni...",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "id_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1Ni...",
  "not-before-policy": 0,

}

5.1 Node.js / TypeScript Example

Using standard fetch to create a user and assign a role via the Admin REST API.

import { fetch } from 'undici'; // or built-in fetch in Node.js 18+

interface KeycloakConfig {
  baseUrl: string;
  adminRealm: string;
  targetRealm: string;
  adminUser: string;
  adminPass: string;
}

const config: KeycloakConfig = {
  baseUrl: process.env.KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL || 'http://127.0.0.1:8180',
  adminRealm: 'master',
  targetRealm: 'gothru',
  adminUser: process.env.KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_USERNAME || 'admin',
  adminPass: process.env.KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD || 'admin',
};

// 1. Get Admin Access Token
async function getAdminToken(): Promise<string> {
  const tokenUrl = `${config.baseUrl}/realms/${config.adminRealm}/protocol/openid-connect/token`;
  const params = new URLSearchParams({
    client_id: 'admin-cli',
    grant_type: 'password',
    username: config.adminUser,
    password: config.adminPass,
  });

  const res = await fetch(tokenUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' },
    body: params.toString(),
  });

  if (!res.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Failed to obtain admin token: ${res.statusText}`);
  }

  const data = (await res.json()) as { access_token: string };
  return data.access_token;
}

// 2. Create User in GoThru Realm
async function createUser(token: string, user: { username: string; email: string; firstName: string; lastName: string }) {
  const usersUrl = `${config.baseUrl}/admin/realms/${config.targetRealm}/users`;
  const res = await fetch(usersUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      username: user.username,
      email: user.email,
      firstName: user.firstName,
      lastName: user.lastName,
      enabled: true,
      emailVerified: true,
    }),
  });

  if (res.status === 201) {
    const location = res.headers.get('location') || '';
    const userId = location.split('/').pop();
    console.log(`User created successfully with ID: ${userId}`);
    return userId;
  } else if (res.status === 409) {
    console.log('User already exists in Keycloak');
  } else {
    throw new Error(`User creation failed: ${res.status} ${res.statusText}`);
  }
}

// Execute
async function run() {
  const token = await getAdminToken();
  await createUser(token, {
    username: 'developer1',
    email: 'developer1@gothru.co',
    firstName: 'Dev',
    lastName: 'GoThru',
  });
}

5.2 Go Example

Verifying a Keycloak Access Token via the Userinfo endpoint in a Go backend service (matches the Panorra API pattern).

package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"time"
)

type KeycloakUserInfo struct {
	Sub               string `json:"sub"`
	EmailVerified     bool   `json:"email_verified"`
	PreferredUsername string `json:"preferred_username"`
	Email             string `json:"email"`
	Name              string `json:"name"`
	GivenName         string `json:"given_name"`
	FamilyName        string `json:"family_name"`
}

type KeycloakService struct {
	BaseURL    string
	Realm      string
	HTTPClient *http.Client
}

func NewKeycloakService(baseURL, realm string) *KeycloakService {
	return &KeycloakService{
		BaseURL: baseURL,
		Realm:   realm,
		HTTPClient: &http.Client{
			Timeout: 10 * time.Second,
		},
	}
}

func (s *KeycloakService) VerifyAccessToken(accessToken string) (*KeycloakUserInfo, error) {
	if accessToken == "" {
		return nil, errors.New("access token is empty")
	}

	userInfoURL := fmt.Sprintf("%s/realms/%s/protocol/openid-connect/userinfo", s.BaseURL, s.Realm)
	req, err := http.NewRequest("GET", userInfoURL, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+accessToken)
	req.Header.Set("Accept", "application/json")

	resp, err := s.HTTPClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to call Keycloak: %w", err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()

	if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusUnauthorized || resp.StatusCode == http.StatusForbidden {
		return nil, errors.New("invalid or expired token")
	}
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		body, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("keycloak returned status %d: %s", resp.StatusCode, string(body))
	}

	var info KeycloakUserInfo
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&info); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to decode userinfo: %w", err)
	}

	return &info, nil
}

func main() {
	svc := NewKeycloakService("https://gothru-sso.web.id", "gothru")
	user, err := svc.VerifyAccessToken("YOUR_TEST_ACCESS_TOKEN")
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("Verification error: %v\n", err)
		return
	}
	fmt.Printf("Authenticated GoThru User: %s (%s, sub=%s)\n", user.PreferredUsername, user.Email, user.Sub)
}

        curl_setopt_array($ch, [
            CURLOPT_POST => true,
            CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS => $payload,
            CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
            CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => ['Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded'],
            CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 15,
        ]);

        $response = curl_exec($ch);
        $status = (int)curl_getinfo($ch, CURLINFO_RESPONSE_CODE);
        curl_close($ch);

        $json = json_decode((string)$response, true);
        if ($status !== 200 || empty($json['access_token'])) {
            throw new RuntimeException("Keycloak login failed with status {$status}");
        }

        $this->token = $json['access_token'];
    }

    public function resetPassword(string $userId, string $newPassword, bool $temporary = false): bool
    {
        $url = "{$this->baseUrl}/admin/realms/{$this->realm}/users/" . rawurlencode($userId) . "/reset-password";
        $payload = json_encode([
            'type' => 'password',
            'value' => $newPassword,
            'temporary' => $temporary,
        ], JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);

        $ch = curl_init($url);
        curl_setopt_array($ch, [
            CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST => 'PUT',
            CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS => $payload,
            CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
            CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => [
                'Authorization: Bearer ' . $this->token,
                'Content-Type: application/json',
            ],
            CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 15,
        ]);

        $response = curl_exec($ch);
        $status = (int)curl_getinfo($ch, CURLINFO_RESPONSE_CODE);
        curl_close($ch);

        return $status === 204;
    }
}

5.4 Python Example

Using requests for client credentials authentication and fetching realm users.

import os
import requests

BASE_URL = os.getenv("KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8180")
REALM = os.getenv("KEYCLOAK_REALM", "gothru")
ADMIN_USER = os.getenv("KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_USERNAME", "admin")
ADMIN_PASS = os.getenv("KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD", "admin")

def get_admin_token() -> str:
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/realms/master/protocol/openid-connect/token"
    data = {
        "client_id": "admin-cli",
        "grant_type": "password",
        "username": ADMIN_USER,
        "password": ADMIN_PASS,
    }
    resp = requests.post(url, data=data, timeout=10)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()["access_token"]

def list_users(token: str, max_results: int = 50):
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/admin/realms/{REALM}/users"
    headers = {
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
        "Accept": "application/json",
    }
    params = {"first": 0, "max": max_results}
    resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=10)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    token = get_admin_token()
    users = list_users(token)
    print(f"Retrieved {len(users)} users from realm '{REALM}':")
    for u in users:
        print(f" - {u.get('username')} <{u.get('email')}> [ID: {u.get('id')}]")

6. HTTP Status Codes & Error Handling

HTTP Status Meaning Typical Cause in Keycloak
200 OK Success Request succeeded and body contains data.
201 Created Resource Created User, client, or role created. Look at Location header for ID.
204 No Content Success (No Body) Update, delete, password reset, or role assignment completed.
400 Bad Request Invalid Request Missing required body, invalid JSON, or invalid parameter values.
401 Unauthorized Invalid Authentication Access token expired, missing Bearer token, or invalid admin credentials.
403 Forbidden Permission Denied The authenticated account lacks necessary realm/admin roles (e.g. manage-users).
404 Not Found Resource Missing User ID, Client UUID, or Role Name does not exist.
409 Conflict Duplicate Resource User with username or email already exists.
502 Bad Gateway Network / Proxy Failure Keycloak instance is unreachable or reverse proxy failed.

7. Security & Best Practices

  1. Never Expose Client Secrets in Frontend:
    • Single Page Applications (Angular, React, Vue) and mobile apps must use public clients with PKCE (S256). Never embed client secrets in client-side code.
  2. Short-Lived Access Tokens:
    • Keep Access Token Lifespan short (e.g., 5 minutes) and use Refresh Tokens to maintain sessions.
  3. Validate JWT Locally When Possible:
    • High-throughput backend APIs should validate tokens locally using JWKS (/certs) with signature and expiry checks rather than hitting /userinfo on every request.
  4. Use sub for User Foreign Keys:
    • Keycloak's sub UUID is immutable. Usernames and emails can be modified by users; always link your local database records to sub.
  5. Use Service Accounts for Machine-to-Machine Integration:
    • Use dedicated client IDs with client_credentials grant rather than sharing admin user credentials.
  6. Paginate List Queries:
    • Always supply first and max query parameters when querying /admin/realms/{realm}/users to prevent performance degradation on large databases (e.g., 55,000+ users).

Implementation: Exclude Public User Profile Route from Auth JWT Middleware

Files Changed

  • src/middleware/auth.go
  • src/routes/v1/route.go
  • src/middleware/auth_test.go (new test file)
  • src/routes/v1/userRoutes_test.go (new test file)

Summary of Implementation

The AuthJWTExclude middleware was updated to support:

  1. Dynamic route parameter pattern matching (e.g. :username).
  2. Explicit auth enforcement rules using the ! prefix (e.g. !GET:/v1/users/detail).
  3. Safe rule parsing so colons in path parameters are not confused with HTTP method separators.

In src/routes/v1/route.go, GET:/v1/users/:username and OPTIONS:/v1/users/:username were registered as excluded routes, while !GET:/v1/users/detail and !GET:/v1/users/me were registered as explicit auth-enforced rules.

Detailed Changes

1. Middleware Enhancement (src/middleware/auth.go)

type excludeRule struct {
	method   string
	path     string
	isPrefix bool
	isNegate bool
}
  • Rule Parsing: Detects ! prefix to flag isNegate = true. Only splits on colon if the colon appears before the first slash (indicating METHOD:path), avoiding corruption of path parameter patterns like /v1/users/:username.
  • Two-Pass Rule Evaluation:
    • Pass 1 (Negate / Require Auth): If any rule with isNegate = true matches the request path and method, authJWT(c) is immediately invoked, guaranteeing auth enforcement.
    • Pass 2 (Exclude / Bypass Auth): If any rule with isNegate = false matches, c.Next() is called to bypass auth.
    • Fallback: Any path not matching an exclude rule defaults to authJWT(c).
  • matchPath Function:
    • Handles prefix matching with isPrefix.
    • Handles exact string equality.
    • Handles :param segment matching by splitting both rule and request paths by /, checking segment counts, and treating :param as matching any single non-empty path segment.

2. Route Configuration (src/routes/v1/route.go)

func SetupRoutes(app *fiber.App) {
	v1 := app.Group("/v1", middleware.AuthJWTExclude(
		...
		"!GET:/v1/users/detail",
		"!GET:/v1/users/me",
		"GET:/v1/users/:username",
		"OPTIONS:/v1/users/:username",
	))
  • GET /v1/users/:username (and OPTIONS) allows public access to the user profile without credentials.
  • GET /v1/users/detail and GET /v1/users/me are protected by the negate rules and require valid JWT tokens.
  • All mutating endpoints (PUT /v1/users/*, PATCH /v1/users/*) require valid JWT tokens.

Verification & Tests

Automated Tests

  1. src/middleware/auth_test.go:
    • TestAuthJWTExclude_ParametricAndPrefixRules: Validates that public routes, wildcard prefix routes, and parameterized routes pass without token; and validates that negated private routes and non-excluded routes return 401 Unauthorized.
    • TestAuthJWT_PopulatesLocalsOnValidToken: Validates that authenticating with a valid JWT populates c.Locals("sub").
  2. src/routes/v1/userRoutes_test.go:
    • TestUserPublicProfileRouteIsExcluded: Verifies GET /v1/users/:username does not return 401 Missing Authorization header.
    • TestUserPrivateRoutesRequireAuth: Verifies all 11 private user routes return 401 Unauthorized without token.
    • TestUserPrivateRoutesPassWithValidAuthToken: Verifies valid JWT token is accepted on /v1/users/detail.
    • TestExistingExclusionsRemainUnaffected: Verifies existing exclusions (/v1/room, /v1/viewers/*, /v1/additional/version/latest, /v1/exhibitions/model) remain public.

Test Execution

go test -v ./src/middleware/...
go test -v ./src/routes/v1/...
go test ./...

All test suites pass successfully.

Overview

Endpoint GET /v1/users/:username is used to retrieve a user's public profile (controllers.GetUser). However, because the entire /v1 group is wrapped by middleware.AuthJWTExclude, this endpoint was previously blocked with 401 Unauthorized ("Missing Authorization header") when accessed without an authentication token.

Problem

  1. GET /v1/users/:username is a public endpoint intended for visitors and frontend profile viewers without requiring login credentials.
  2. middleware.AuthJWTExclude previously only performed literal string equality (reqPath == rule.path) or prefix matching (isPrefix). A parameterized path pattern like GET:/v1/users/:username was treated as a literal string and failed to match dynamic username paths (e.g. /v1/users/johndoe).
  3. Under the same /v1/users route prefix, there are private endpoints that MUST require authentication:
    • GET /v1/users/detail (user's personal data, settings, billing)
    • GET /v1/users/me (checks authenticated identity against session)
    • PUT /v1/users/detail, PUT /v1/users/info, PUT /v1/users/profile, PUT /v1/users/setting
    • PATCH /v1/users/deactivate, PATCH /v1/users/is-back, PATCH /v1/users/fav-colors, PATCH /v1/users/json-version, PATCH /v1/users/avatar
  4. Naively adding a wildcard rule like GET:/v1/users/* would bypass JWT verification for /v1/users/detail and /v1/users/me, preventing JWT claim population (c.Locals("sub")) and breaking authenticated requests.

Goals

  1. Allow unauthenticated public access to GET /v1/users/:username and OPTIONS /v1/users/:username.
  2. Ensure all other endpoints under /v1/users (especially GET /v1/users/detail and GET /v1/users/me) strictly require a valid JWT token.
  3. Keep all existing exclusions (/v1/room, /v1/viewers/*, POST:/v1/auth, GET:/v1/exhibitions/model, etc.) 100% unaffected.
  4. Provide comprehensive unit and route integration tests.

Scope

In scope:

  • src/middleware/auth.go (enhance AuthJWTExclude with path parameter matching and explicit negate/enforce rules)
  • src/routes/v1/route.go (register exclusion and negate rules)
  • src/middleware/auth_test.go (unit tests for middleware pattern matching and authentication enforcement)
  • src/routes/v1/userRoutes_test.go (integration tests for public and private routes)

Out of scope:

  • Changes to controllers.GetUser or user model/database schemas.
  • Changes to private user action handlers.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. GET /v1/users/:username succeeds without an Authorization header.
  2. OPTIONS /v1/users/:username succeeds without an Authorization header.
  3. GET /v1/users/detail returns 401 Unauthorized ("Missing Authorization header") when called without a token.
  4. GET /v1/users/me returns 401 Unauthorized ("Missing Authorization header") when called without a token.
  5. All PUT and PATCH endpoints under /v1/users require authentication.
  6. Valid JWT tokens on private endpoints properly populate c.Locals("sub") and c.Locals("ls").
  7. All existing excluded routes remain completely unaffected.
  8. All unit and route integration tests pass (go test ./...).

Implementation Summary

Implemented the reader detail endpoint for marketing blog articles. Fetches published articles by unique slug, increments views_count in a background goroutine, returns the Editor.js content payload, author profile, and dynamically populates up to 4 related articles from the same category or latest posts.

Key Code Logic (src/action/v1/blog/getPublicArticle.go)

func GetPublicArticle(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
	slug := c.Params("slug")
	if slug == "" {
		return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{Status: fiber.StatusBadRequest, Messages: "Article slug is required"})
	}

	var article models.BlogArticle
	err := config.DB.Preload("Author").Preload("Category").
		Where("slug = ? AND status = ?", slug, "published").
		First(&article).Error

	if err != nil {
		if errors.Is(err, gorm.ErrRecordNotFound) {
			return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{Status: fiber.StatusNotFound, Messages: "Article not found"})
		}
		return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{Status: fiber.StatusInternalServerError, Messages: "Database error: " + err.Error()})
	}

	// Asynchronous view count increment
	go func(id string) {
		config.DB.Model(&models.BlogArticle{}).
			Where("id = ?", id).
			UpdateColumn("views_count", gorm.Expr("views_count + 1"))
	}(article.ID.String())

	// Fetch up to 4 related articles
	var relatedRaw []models.BlogArticle
	relatedQuery := config.DB.Model(&models.BlogArticle{}).
		Where("status = ? AND id != ?", "published", article.ID)
	if article.CategoryID != nil {
		relatedQuery = relatedQuery.Where("category_id = ?", article.CategoryID)
	}
	_ = relatedQuery.Order("published_at DESC").Limit(4).Find(&relatedRaw).Error

	// Response formatting...
}

  • View counter increases non-blockingly without delaying response time.

func GetBlogAsset(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
	fileName := filepath.Clean(c.Params("file_name"))
	if strings.Contains(fileName, "..") {
		return c.SendStatus(fiber.StatusBadRequest)
	}

	baseDir := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("DIRECTORY_IMAGES"))
	if baseDir == "" {
		baseDir = strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("DIRECTORY_ASSET"))
	}
	if baseDir == "" {
		baseDir = "uploads"
	}

	filePath := filepath.Join(baseDir, "blog", fileName)
	if _, err := os.Stat(filePath); os.IsNotExist(err) {
		return c.SendStatus(fiber.StatusNotFound)
	}

	return c.SendFile(filePath)
}

  • Uses filepath.Clean and checks for .. sequences to prevent directory traversal outside the blog upload folder.
  • Uses Fiber's SendFile to automatically infer and set the appropriate MIME type header (image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, etc.).

func ListPublicArticles(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
	page, limit, offset := ParsePagination(c.Query("page"), c.Query("limit"), 10, 50)
	search := strings.TrimSpace(c.Query("search"))
	categoryQuery := strings.TrimSpace(c.Query("category"))
	tagQuery := strings.TrimSpace(c.Query("tag"))
	featuredQuery := strings.TrimSpace(c.Query("featured"))

	query := config.DB.Model(&models.BlogArticle{}).
		Preload("Author").
		Preload("Category").
		Where("status = ?", "published")

	if search != "" {
		searchLike := "%" + search + "%"
		query = query.Where("(title ILIKE ? OR excerpt ILIKE ? OR seo_keywords ILIKE ?)", searchLike, searchLike, searchLike)
	}

	if categoryQuery != "" {
		if catID, err := uuid.Parse(categoryQuery); err == nil {
			query = query.Where("category_id = ?", catID)
		} else {
			var cat models.BlogCategory
			if err := config.DB.Select("id").Where("slug = ?", categoryQuery).First(&cat).Error; err == nil {
				query = query.Where("category_id = ?", cat.ID)
			} else {
				return helpers.SendSuccess(c, helpers.SuccessOpts{
					Status:   fiber.StatusOK,
					Messages: "Public articles list",
					Data: fiber.Map{
						"articles":    []publicArticleListItem{},
						"total":       0,
						"page":        page,
						"limit":       limit,
						"total_pages": 0,
					},
				})
			}
		}
	}

	if tagQuery != "" {
		query = query.Where("tags::text ILIKE ?", "%\""+tagQuery+"\"%")
	}

	if strings.EqualFold(featuredQuery, "true") || featuredQuery == "1" {
		query = query.Where("is_featured = ?", true)
	}

	var total int64
	_ = query.Count(&total)

	var articles []models.BlogArticle
	if total > 0 {
		_ = query.Order("is_featured DESC, published_at DESC, created_at DESC").
			Limit(limit).Offset(offset).Find(&articles)
	}
	// Items mapping and return envelope
}

func ListPublicTags(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
	var rawTagsList []json.RawMessage

	if err := config.DB.Model(&models.BlogArticle{}).
		Where("status = ?", "published").
		Pluck("tags", &rawTagsList).Error; err != nil {
		return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{
			Status:   fiber.StatusInternalServerError,
			Messages: "Failed to fetch tags: " + err.Error(),
		})
	}

	seen := make(map[string]struct{})
	tags := make([]string, 0)

	for _, raw := range rawTagsList {
		var itemTags []string
		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &itemTags); err == nil {
			for _, tag := range itemTags {
				if tag == "" {
					continue
				}
				if _, exists := seen[tag]; !exists {
					seen[tag] = struct{}{}
					tags = append(tags, tag)
				}
			}
		}
	}

	return helpers.SendSuccess(c, helpers.SuccessOpts{
		Status:   fiber.StatusOK,
		Messages: "Public tags list",
		Data:     fiber.Map{"tags": tags},
	})
}

func SupportListCategories(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
	lastLogin, _ := c.Locals("ls").(string)
	encryptStr, _ := c.Locals("sub").(string)

	var categories []models.BlogCategory
	if err := config.DB.Order("name ASC").Find(&categories).Error; err != nil {
		return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{Status: fiber.StatusInternalServerError, Messages: "Failed to fetch categories: " + err.Error()})
	}

	type catCount struct {
		CategoryID string `gorm:"column:category_id"`
		Total      int64  `gorm:"column:total"`
	}
	var counts []catCount
	config.DB.Model(&models.BlogArticle{}).
		Select("category_id, count(*) as total").
		Group("category_id").
		Scan(&counts)

	countMap := make(map[string]int64)
	for _, cc := range counts {
		countMap[cc.CategoryID] = cc.Total
	}

	result := make([]supportCategoryItem, 0, len(categories))
	for _, cat := range categories {
		desc := ""
		if cat.Description != nil {
			desc = *cat.Description
		}
		result = append(result, supportCategoryItem{
			ID:            cat.ID.String(),
			Name:          cat.Name,
			Slug:          cat.Slug,
			Description:   desc,
			ArticlesCount: countMap[cat.ID.String()],
			CreatedAt:     cat.CreatedAt.Format("2006-01-02 15:04:05"),
		})
	}

	return helpers.SendSuccess(c, helpers.SuccessOpts{
		Status:     fiber.StatusOK,
		Messages:   "Categories list",
		Data:       fiber.Map{"categories": result},
		Encrypt:    true,

func SupportPublishArticle(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
	idParam := c.Params("id")
	articleUUID, err := uuid.Parse(idParam)
	if err != nil {
		return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{Status: fiber.StatusBadRequest, Messages: "Invalid article ID"})
	}

	var article models.BlogArticle
	if err := config.DB.First(&article, "id = ?", articleUUID).Error; err != nil {
		if errors.Is(err, gorm.ErrRecordNotFound) {
			return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{Status: fiber.StatusNotFound, Messages: "Article not found"})
		}
		return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{Status: fiber.StatusInternalServerError, Messages: "Database error: " + err.Error()})
	}

	var req publishArticleRequest
	_ = c.BodyParser(&req)

	shouldPublish := true
	if req.Publish != nil {
		shouldPublish = *req.Publish
	} else {
		shouldPublish = article.Status != "published"
	}

	if shouldPublish {
		article.Status = "published"

Key Code Logic (src/action/v1/blog/supportUploadImage.go)

func SupportUploadImage(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
	fileHeader, fileErr := c.FormFile("image")
	if fileErr != nil || fileHeader == nil {
		fileHeader, fileErr = c.FormFile("file")
		if fileErr != nil || fileHeader == nil {
			return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{
				Status:   fiber.StatusBadRequest,
				Messages: "Image file is required (form field: 'image' or 'file')",
			})
		}
	}

	ext := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimPrefix(filepath.Ext(fileHeader.Filename), "."))
	if ext != "jpg" && ext != "jpeg" && ext != "png" && ext != "webp" && ext != "gif" {
		return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{
			Status:   fiber.StatusBadRequest,
			Messages: "Image extension not allowed. Supported: jpg, jpeg, png, webp, gif",
		})
	}

	if fileHeader.Size > 10*1024*1024 {
		return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{Status: fiber.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge, Messages: "Image too large, maximum size is 10MB"})
	}

	baseDir := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("DIRECTORY_IMAGES"))
	if baseDir == "" {
		baseDir = strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("DIRECTORY_ASSET"))
	}
	if baseDir == "" {
		baseDir = "uploads"
	}

	blogDir := filepath.Join(baseDir, "blog")
	_ = os.MkdirAll(blogDir, 0o755)

	filename, _ := helpers.RandomHexFilename(ext)
	dst := filepath.Join(blogDir, filename)
	_ = c.SaveFile(fileHeader, dst)

	appURL := strings.TrimRight(os.Getenv("APP_URL"), "/")
	var imageURL string
	if appURL != "" {
		imageURL = fmt.Sprintf("%s/v1/asset/blog/%s", appURL, filename)
	} else {
		imageURL = fmt.Sprintf("/v1/asset/blog/%s", filename)
	}

	// Editor.js Image Tool response contract
	return c.Status(fiber.StatusOK).JSON(fiber.Map{
		"success": 1,
		"file": fiber.Map{
			"url": imageURL,
		},
		"data": fiber.Map{
			"url":      imageURL,
			"filename": filename,
		},
		"messages": "Image uploaded successfully",
	})
}

package models

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"time"

	"github.com/google/uuid"
	"gorm.io/gorm"
)

type BlogArticle struct {
	ID             uuid.UUID       `gorm:"type:uuid;default:gen_random_uuid();primaryKey" json:"id"`
	AuthorID       uuid.UUID       `gorm:"type:uuid;not null;index"                       json:"author_id"`
	CategoryID     *uuid.UUID      `gorm:"type:uuid;index"                                json:"category_id"`
	Title          string          `gorm:"type:varchar(255);not null"                     json:"title"`
	Slug           string          `gorm:"type:varchar(300);not null;uniqueIndex"         json:"slug"`
	Excerpt        *string         `gorm:"type:text"                                      json:"excerpt"`
	Content        json.RawMessage `gorm:"type:jsonb;not null;default:'{}'::jsonb"        json:"content"`
	CoverImage     *string         `gorm:"type:text"                                      json:"cover_image"`
	Tags           json.RawMessage `gorm:"type:jsonb;not null;default:'[]'::jsonb"        json:"tags"`
	Status         string          `gorm:"type:varchar(20);not null;default:'draft'"      json:"status"`
	IsFeatured     bool            `gorm:"not null;default:false;index"                   json:"is_featured"`
	SEOTitle       *string         `gorm:"type:varchar(255)"                              json:"seo_title"`
	SEODescription *string         `gorm:"type:text"                                      json:"seo_description"`
	SEOKeywords    *string         `gorm:"type:text"                                      json:"seo_keywords"`
	PublishedAt    *time.Time      `gorm:"type:timestamp with time zone"                  json:"published_at"`
	ViewsCount     int64           `gorm:"not null;default:0"                             json:"views_count"`
	CreatedAt      time.Time       `gorm:"autoCreateTime"                                 json:"created_at"`
	UpdatedAt      time.Time       `gorm:"autoUpdateTime"                                 json:"updated_at"`

	Author   *User         `gorm:"foreignKey:AuthorID;references:ID"   json:"author,omitempty"`
	Category *BlogCategory `gorm:"foreignKey:CategoryID;references:ID" json:"category,omitempty"`
}

func (a *BlogArticle) TableName() string {
	return "blog_articles"
}

func (a *BlogArticle) BeforeCreate(tx *gorm.DB) error {
	if a.ID == uuid.Nil {
		a.ID = uuid.New()
	}
	if len(a.Content) == 0 {
		a.Content = json.RawMessage(`{}`)
	}
	if len(a.Tags) == 0 {
		a.Tags = json.RawMessage(`[]`)
	}
	return nil
}

Behavior

  • Automatically defaults Content to {} and Tags to [] when creating articles.
  • Cascading delete on author account deletion (users.id).
  • Sets category_id to NULL if associated category is deleted, ensuring article preservation.

issues.display_title: Issue #212: Fix Update Password API for Google OAuth / Passwordless Users
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Fix Update Password API for Google OAuth / Passwordless Users

Files Changed

  • src/action/v1/auth/updatePassword.go: Modified request struct and password update logic.
  • src/helpers/user.go: Enhanced GetAuthUser with c.Locals("auth_user") support and nil-safe type assertions.
  • src/action/v1/auth/updatePassword_test.go: Added test suite covering Google users, standard users, validation errors, and auth failures.

Resolution Strategy

  1. Nullable Pointer Field (*string):
    CurrentPassword in UpdatePasswordRequest was changed from string with tag validate:"required" to *string without a struct-level required tag. This allows JSON null, empty string, or omitted keys to parse cleanly without triggering validator parse rejections.

  2. Early Authentication & Context Inspection:
    helpers.GetAuthUser(c) is called right after body parsing to check whether the user has a password in the database:

    hasPassword := user.Password != ""

  3. Dynamic Requirement Enforcement:

    • If hasPassword == true: req.CurrentPassword is required. If nil or empty string, a 400 Bad Request with message "Required input body| current_password, new_password, confirm_password" is returned.
    • If hasPassword == false: req.CurrentPassword is optional. The validation message for new_password and confirm_password defaults to "Required input body| new_password, confirm_password".

  4. Conditional MD5 Verification:
    The current password hash verification is only performed when hasPassword == true:

    if hasPassword {
    currSum := md5.Sum([]byte(*req.CurrentPassword))
    currHashed := hex.EncodeToString(currSum[:])
    if currHashed != user.Password {
        return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{Status: fiber.StatusConflict, Messages: "Current password not match"})
    }
}

    Users without a password skip this check completely.

  5. Safe Database Update:
    Guarded config.DB != nil before executing config.DB.Model(user).Updates(...) to allow unit testing without a live database instance.

  6. Enhanced GetAuthUser Helper:
    src/helpers/user.go was updated to:

    • Check c.Locals("auth_user") for preloaded mock users in tests.
    • Safely extract c.Locals("sub") with a type check instead of an unchecked type assertion that could panic on unauthenticated requests.

Detailed Code Changes

1. src/action/v1/auth/updatePassword.go

type UpdatePasswordRequest struct {
-	CurrentPassword string `json:"current_password" validate:"required"`
-	NewPassword     string `json:"new_password"     validate:"required"`
-	ConfirmPassword string `json:"confirm_password" validate:"required"`
+	CurrentPassword *string `json:"current_password"`
+	NewPassword     string  `json:"new_password"     validate:"required"`
+	ConfirmPassword string  `json:"confirm_password" validate:"required"`
}

func UpdatePassword(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
 	var req UpdatePasswordRequest
 	if err := c.BodyParser(&req); err != nil {
 		return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{Status: fiber.StatusBadRequest, Messages: "Invalid request body"})
 	}
 
+	user, err := helpers.GetAuthUser(c)
+	if err != nil || user == nil {
+		return err // helpers.GetAuthUser already sends Error response
+	}
+
+	hasPassword := user.Password != ""
+	reqMsg := "Required input body| current_password, new_password, confirm_password"
+	if !hasPassword {
+		reqMsg = "Required input body| new_password, confirm_password"
+	}
+
+	// If the user already has a password, current_password is required
+	if hasPassword && (req.CurrentPassword == nil || *req.CurrentPassword == "") {
+		return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{Status: fiber.StatusBadRequest, Messages: reqMsg})
+	}
+
 	// Validate required fields

Overview

Endpoint POST /v1/auth/password (controllers.UpdatePassword) allows authenticated users to set or change their account password. Users who register via Google OAuth (or other third-party OAuth providers) do not have an initial password stored in the database (user.Password == ""). When such users attempt to set a password for the first time by passing current_password: null (or an empty/omitted current password), the API previously returned 400 Bad Request.

Problem & Root Cause Analysis

  1. Strict Required Validation Tag:
    The request struct UpdatePasswordRequest defined CurrentPassword with validate:"required":

    type UpdatePasswordRequest struct {
    CurrentPassword string `json:"current_password" validate:"required"`
    NewPassword     string `json:"new_password"     validate:"required"`
    ConfirmPassword string `json:"confirm_password" validate:"required"`
}

    When a user sends payload:

    {
    "current_password": null,
    "new_password": "1234567trCD",
    "confirm_password": "1234567trCD"
}

    The validator flagged current_password as missing/empty and immediately rejected the request with 400 Bad Request:

    {
    "data": {
        "errors": {
            "input": " current_password, new_password, confirm_password",
            "messages": "Required input body"
        },
        "status": "BAD_REQUEST",
        "valid": false
    },
    "statusCode": 400
}

  2. Unconditional Current Password Verification:

    currSum := md5.Sum([]byte(req.CurrentPassword))
currHashed := hex.EncodeToString(currSum[:])
if currHashed != user.Password {
    return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{Status: fiber.StatusConflict, Messages: "Current password not match"})
}

    For OAuth users where user.Password == "", comparing MD5("") (d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e) against "" would always evaluate to not equal and fail with 409 Conflict ("Current password not match").

Goals

  1. Allow users without an existing password (user.Password == "") to set their account password with current_password being null, empty string "", or omitted.
  2. Maintain strict current_password requirements and MD5 hash verification for users who already have an established password (user.Password != "").
  3. Ensure input validation messages appropriately reflect whether current_password is expected.
  4. Support safe user retrieval and mockable user context for testing without requiring live database connections.
  5. Provide comprehensive unit tests covering OAuth user scenarios, standard user scenarios, validation errors, and authentication failures.

Scope

In scope:

  • src/action/v1/auth/updatePassword.go: Make CurrentPassword optional when user.Password == "", validate dynamically based on password status, and skip old password verification for passwordless accounts.
  • src/helpers/user.go: Support c.Locals("auth_user") mock injection and nil-safe extraction of c.Locals("sub").
  • src/action/v1/auth/updatePassword_test.go: Unit tests for all password update workflows.

Out of scope:

  • Changes to user registration flows (registerUser.go, authGoogle.go).
  • Changes to OTP-based password reset (resetPassword.go).
  • Database schema changes.

    • Sending mismatched new_password and confirm_password returns 409 Conflict ("Password not same").
    • Missing new_password or confirm_password returns 400 Bad Request ("Required input body| new_password, confirm_password").
  2. When user.Password != "":

    • Sending an incorrect current_password returns 409 Conflict ("Current password not match").
    • Sending matching valid current_password and new passwords updates the password in DB and returns 200 OK.
  3. Unauthenticated requests return 401 Unauthorized.

issues.display_title: Issue #217: Handle Miss Worker Caused by Unprovisioned Dev Environment
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Fix Viewer JSON Worker Infinite Requeue Loop & Miss Worker Handling

Files Changed

  • src/workers/viewer_json.go
  • src/workers/worker.go
  • src/workers/workers_test.go (new)

Resolution Strategy

  1. Requeue Loop Prevention in Consumer Engine (src/workers/worker.go):

    • Inspect msg.Redelivered. If a message fails after having already been redelivered, discard it using msg.Nack(false, false).
    • Apply a 1-second backoff delay on the first failure (!msg.Redelivered) before requeueing with msg.Nack(false, true) to eliminate high-frequency CPU/DB spinning.

  2. Miss Worker & Record Not Found Handling (src/workers/viewer_json.go):

    • When a job references an exhibition that does not exist in the database (e.g. from a miss worker or deleted record), GORM returns gorm.ErrRecordNotFound.
    • The handler checks errors.Is(err, gorm.ErrRecordNotFound). If matched, it logs that the record was not found and returns nil, allowing the message to be acknowledged (Ack) and permanently cleared from the queue.
    • Malformed JSON payloads that fail json.Unmarshal are also skipped (return nil) rather than returned as errors.

  3. Automated Unit Testing (src/workers/workers_test.go):

    • Added unit tests verifying that malformed payloads and empty exhibition IDs are safely acknowledged without returning errors.

Code Changes

1. Consumer Engine Anti-Loop (src/workers/worker.go)

if err := w.Handle(ctx, msg); err != nil {
    log.Printf("❌ Worker %q handle error: %v", queue, err)
    if msg.Redelivered {
        log.Printf("⚠️  Worker %q message already redelivered — discarding to prevent infinite loop", queue)
        _ = msg.Nack(false, false)
    } else {
        time.Sleep(1 * time.Second)
        _ = msg.Nack(false, true)
    }
} else {
    _ = msg.Ack(false)
}

2. Miss Worker & Record Not Found Handling (src/workers/viewer_json.go)

func (w *ViewerJSONWorker) Handle(ctx context.Context, msg amqp.Delivery) error {
    _ = ctx

    var payload queues.ViewerJSONPayload
    if err := json.Unmarshal(msg.Body, &payload); err != nil {
        log.Printf("[ViewerJSONWorker] unmarshal error: %v — skipping invalid payload", err)
        return nil
    }

    exhibitionID := strings.TrimSpace(payload.ExhibitionID)
    if exhibitionID == "" {
        log.Printf("[ViewerJSONWorker] missing exhibition_id — skipping")
        return nil
    }

    log.Printf("[ViewerJSONWorker] start exhibition_id=%s", exhibitionID)
    if err := exhibition.WriteViewerJSONFromDiskAndRedis(exhibitionID); err != nil {
        if errors.Is(err, gorm.ErrRecordNotFound) {
            log.Printf("[ViewerJSONWorker] exhibition_id=%s not found in DB — skipping job", exhibitionID)
            return nil
        }
        log.Printf("[ViewerJSONWorker] failed exhibition_id=%s: %v", exhibitionID, err)
        return err
    }

    log.Printf("[ViewerJSONWorker] done exhibition_id=%s", exhibitionID)
    return nil
}

Behavior and Recovery

  • Automatic Queue Clearance:
    When workers are restarted with the new code, stuck messages caused by miss worker events are consumed once, recognized as record not found, logged, and immediately acknowledged (Ack). The queue drains cleanly without manual purging.
  • Fail-Safe Operation:
    Even if environment variables (RabbitMQ host / queue prefix) are misconfigured or unprovisioned, workers will never enter a high-throughput infinite loop that degrades server performance.

Verification

Output:

2026/09/25 08:07:37 [ViewerJSONWorker] unmarshal error: invalid character 'o' in literal null (expecting 'u') — skipping invalid payload
--- PASS: TestViewerJSONWorker_Handle_MalformedJSON (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestViewerJSONWorker_Handle_EmptyExhibitionID
2026/09/25 08:07:37 [ViewerJSONWorker] missing exhibition_id — skipping
--- PASS: TestViewerJSONWorker_Handle_EmptyExhibitionID (0.00s)
PASS

Build Verification

go build ./cmd/worker-viewer-json

Compiles cleanly with zero errors.

Overview

The background worker service (worker-viewer-json and worker.go) processes asynchronous queue messages for rebuilding viewer.json files for exhibitions. The system experienced a critical issue where workers entered a high-frequency requeue loop (~950+ req/sec) repeatedly failing with record not found and exhausting CPU and database resources.

Problem & Root Cause Analysis

  1. Miss Worker Due to Missing / Unisolated Dev Environment:

    • A dedicated, isolated RabbitMQ environment for Development had not yet been provisioned.
    • Consequently, the Dev server connected to the Live RabbitMQ broker (192.168.1.55) and consumed from the Live queue (villume_live-viewer-json), while remaining connected to the Development database (villume_db_dev on 192.168.1.202).
    • This caused a miss worker condition (cross-environment worker mismatch):
      • Jobs published with Live exhibition IDs were consumed by the Dev worker, or Dev exhibition IDs were queued into the Live queue.
      • When queried against the wrong database, the query returned [rows:0] resulting in gorm.ErrRecordNotFound (record not found).

  2. Severe Infinite Requeue Loop:

    • In src/workers/worker.go, the message consumer loop unconditionally responded to any handler error with: 
      if err := w.Handle(ctx, msg); err != nil {
    log.Printf("❌ Worker %q handle error: %v", queue, err)
    _ = msg.Nack(false, true) // requeue = true
}
    • RabbitMQ immediately pushed the rejected message back to the front of the queue without delay or retry limits.
    • The worker immediately re-consumed the same message, triggering an infinite hot loop of ~950–1000 deliveries per second, saturating database connections, disk I/O, and CPU.

Goals

  1. Eliminate Requeue Loops Completely:

    • Prevent any message from looping infinitely upon failure.
    • Guard against repeated redeliveries (msg.Redelivered) by rejecting failed messages without requeue (requeue = false), cleanly removing them from the queue.
    • Add backoff delay on initial retry attempts to suppress CPU/DB traffic spikes during transient issues.

  2. Resilient Worker Handling for Miss Worker Scenarios:

    • Provide worker-level resilience even if environment isolation has not yet been fully configured or if a miss worker event occurs.
    • For permanent errors like record not found (gorm.ErrRecordNotFound) in ViewerJSONWorker, log the event and acknowledge (Ack) the message to drop it without requeueing.
    • Silently skip malformed or corrupted JSON payloads in workers instead of returning errors to the requeue loop.

Scope

  • src/workers/viewer_json.go: Handle record not found and unmarshal errors as non-requeueable jobs.
  • src/workers/worker.go: Implement redelivery guards and backoff in the consumer loop to prevent infinite requeuing.
  • src/workers/email.go: Safely skip unmarshal errors without triggering requeue.
  • src/workers/workers_test.go: Automated unit tests verifying worker error and payload handling.

Overview

The worker-email service processes asynchronous transactional email jobs (registration, OTP, password reset, billing receipts, subscription reminders, and contact forms). Previously, the queue name was hardcoded as "villume-mail" across EmailWorker and all 16 publishing endpoints in the codebase.

Problem & Root Cause Analysis

  1. Cross-Environment Queue Collision:

    • Because "villume-mail" was hardcoded without environment prefixing (unlike ViewerJSONQueue()), Development and Live environments connected to the same RabbitMQ broker contended for the identical queue.
    • Live transactional emails were picked up by Dev workers, and Dev test emails were picked up by Live workers.
